correctness.rationale: The \(\mathbb Z^r\)-graded polynomial algebra has nonzero homogeneous polynomials \(F_i\) of independent primitive basis degrees. The explicit scaling action and inverse identify \(D(\prod_iF_i)\) scheme-theoretically with \(V(F_1-1,\ldots,F_r-1)\times(\mathbb G_m)^r\). The left-hand coordinate ring is a domain; hence \(S/J\) injects into a Laurent domain and \(J\) is prime. Integral basis weights yield Euler derivations \(E_a(F_b)=\delta_{ab}F_b\), giving Jacobian rank \(r\) along \(V(J)\); thus the scheme is smooth of codimension \(r\). For the source’s unimodular block matrices \(M=(R;A)\), \(M^{-1}=(B\ K)\), the identities \(RK=0\) and \(AK=I_r\) show every homogenized exponent \(R^\mathsf{T}m+a_i\) has \(K^\mathsf{T}\)-degree \(e_i\). A parametrized dense-torus point ensures no \(u_j\) lies in \(J\), so \(J\) equals its coordinate saturation and the source’s Corollary 3.10 ideal. Bundled `checker.py` was executed at its actual package path and returned `VERIFY_OK` on the exact pentagon example; the general scheme proof, not that finite check, establishes the universal result. Nonprimitive boundary \(F=u^2\), \(\deg u=1\), shows the integral basis hypothesis cannot simply be dropped.

originality.rationale: The initiating paper explicitly leaves \(I(U)=(f_1^h-1,\ldots,f_r^h-1)\) as Conjecture 3.11 while proving only the coordinate saturation. Its unimodularity lemma and Cox-homogeneity premise do not themselves establish the global scheme isomorphism \(D(\prod_i f_i^h)\simeq V(f_i^h-1)\times(\mathbb G_m)^r\), which supplies the missing boundary control. The finite-representation-type paper of Arkani-Hamed et al. proves primeness only for its own family, using boundary-specific Lemma 9.1 after localization; Theorem 5.3 is a related *fully coordinate-localized* analogue. Full-text and statement-implication comparisons revealed no theorem already asserting the all-unimodular-toric conclusion. The new contribution is the global pre-coordinate-boundary slice; the underlying torus action and grading are classical.
residual_risks: General graded-ring decompositions and diagonalizable-group slices are classical; an older explicit global F_i=1 theorem may exist under different terminology, despite this source explicitly leaving its application conjectural.

The authors’ Theorem 3.7 plus Corollary 3.9 supply geometric context from which the answer is now deducible when augmented by the global basis-character argument; the boundary argument is the new content.
Searches do not establish novelty of an unpublished proof or comprehensively index all historical algebraic invariant-theory literature.

value.rationale: The universal claim resolves the precise algebraic gap identified as Conjecture 3.11 in an ongoing 2026 toric positive-chart construction, including the explicit permutahedral example where the computational saturation was inconclusive. Its direct product decomposition shows why all extraneous coordinate-boundary components disappear, improves the proposed procedure by eliminating Gröbner saturation altogether, and supplies smooth complete-intersection geometry. It is not a routine table recalculation; the primitive character mechanism has a clear sharp boundary and applies to the full mathematically motivated class.
